Content covers: the klal-uprat structural reading of 'and to within the curtain, and he shall serve' distinguishing giving-type from removal-type service (l01), the parallel reading of the repeated 'and he shall serve' distinguishing complete service from one followed by another (l03), the verse's second 'and he shall serve' as a genuine repetition rather than redundancy (l06), Rava's open question about a removal-service performed in the Sanctuary itself (l07), the resolution from the doubled 'within'/'and to within' phrasing (l09a), the chain of 'but if so' escalations testing whether a non-priest performing table-arranging, spoonful-arranging, candelabrum-arranging, wick-placing, and oil-placing would be liable to death, each turned back by identifying a further sub-step that is not itself a complete service (l09b, l12), the beraita teaching that kindling the small flame specifically (not general kindling) requires a valid priest in sacred vessels, and the priestly-garment count derived from 'the priests' vs 'the sons of Aaron, the priests' (l15), the parallel escalation for wood-arranging and two-log-arranging turned back by the further step of limb-arranging (l20), Rav and Rabbi Yochanan's explicit dispute over whether two-log-arranging is itself a complete service or merely the start of the wood-arranging service (l23), the beraita following Rav's view listing the services carrying the death penalty for a non-priest - blood-tossing, sprinklings, draining, and the various libations (l26), the parallel beraita following Levi's view - ash-removal, the seven inner sprinklings, and placing any item (valid or invalid) on the altar (l31), and the mishnah's transition into the daily lottery: why a lottery is held at all, why held repeatedly, Rabbi Yochanan's reason (to let the whole Courtyard hear the multitude), the dispute over what garments the lottery participants wore, and Rav Nachman's and Rav Sheshet's respective concerns about strong-armed men seizing the service versus eager volunteers rushing to serve without a proper lottery, closing with the mishnah about handing attendants over to be stripped of their garments (l35, l37, l39, l41, l43). The truncated single-word fragment on the final line ('sheh-lo', 'those who did not') is confirmed via modules/yoma/assets/talmuddev/25a.json's first raw Rashi line ('those who did not merit the lottery: they would strip the sacred garments...') to be the genuine truncated opening of Rashi's comment continuing onto 25a, correctly linked to l43 (the Mishnah quote about handing over to the attendants). A severe consolidation bug was caught and fully corrected before this file was ever written: my first draft of the build script had only 62 entries instead of the required 65, and a byte-exact reread against the raw dictionary revealed that entries from roughly raw line 26 onward had progressively drifted by one to three lines, with several entries silently combining two raw lines' worth of Hebrew content into a single declared vilnaLine (for example, an early draft's entry for vilnaLine 50 actually contained English translating content that only appears on raw lines 52-53). Rather than patch the drifted draft, I discarded it entirely and rebuilt all 65 entries from scratch by fetching the local Gemara segments fresh via make_rashi_work_packet.py, then walking every raw line in order with explicit word-count majority decisions at every boundary (for example raw line 5 'umotzian: i hachi... mibeit' splits 1 word closing l01 against 5 words opening l03, correctly assigned to l03 by strict majority; raw line 53 'sidur echad hu: zerikat dam.' splits 3 words closing l23 against 2 words opening l26, correctly assigned to l23 by strict majority with the 'zerikat dam' opening swallowed and picked back up as the first words of l26 on the next raw line).
